samples.summary: Tooltip text change (`"<name> (self-reported)"`) has no test
samples.evidence: `BlameMarker.toDOM` changed `span.title = this.label` to `` `${this.label} (self-reported)` ``, a user-visible string change. Every gutter assertion in packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.test.ts reads only `el.textContent` (`gutterLabels`, lines 21-25, used at 126/137/158/177/187); nothing anywhere asserts on `title` or the substring "self-reported" (grep for `title|self-reported` over packages/notes returns only the source line and unrelated mermaid/preview hits). The qualifier could be silently dropped or reworded and the suite would stay green.
searchedFor: grep for '.title' assertions in notes tests

samples.summary: Write-path sanitization in `editText` is untested (indistinguishable from read-path sanitization by any existing assertion)
samples.evidence: `editText` now writes `sanitizeAuthor(this.localAuthorName()) ?? ''` into the CRDT, described as "sanitized on the way in as well as on the way out". No test observes the raw stored attribute: all author assertions go through `getAuthorSpans()`, which sanitizes again, so removing the inbound `sanitizeAuthor(...)` call entirely would keep every test in yorkie-note-store.test.ts green. Grepping the frontend notes tests for `values()`/`attributes` finds no test that inspects `doc.getRoot().content.values()` directly, and there is no test that sets a presence name containing control/bidi characters at all.
searchedFor: grep presence.set usages in the test file

samples.summary: `sanitizeWrittenAt`'s reject branch (non-number / non-finite / <= 0) has no direct test
samples.evidence: `sanitizeWrittenAt` returns 0 for a `t` that is not a positive finite number, i.e. NaN/Infinity/negative/string. The only new timestamp test (yorkie-note-store.test.ts:233-245) covers the clamp branch with `t: 4e15`; the pre-existing legacy test (line 184) covers the *absent* attribute case. No test writes `{a: 'x', t: -1}`, `t: NaN`, or `t: 'soon'`, so a regression that let a negative or NaN `at` through — which would corrupt the "newest run wins" comparison in `authorOfRange` — would not be caught.
searchedFor: grep for 'NaN|Infinity|-1' in the frontend notes tests

samples.summary: The clamp test asserts only `at <= Date.now()`, not that clamping preserves a usable timestamp or that the forged run loses the label
samples.evidence: `expect(forged.at).toBeLessThanOrEqual(Date.now())` would also pass if `sanitizeWrittenAt` returned 0, or a negative number, for every input — it pins only an upper bound. The stated rationale ("clamping to now reduces a forged timestamp to a tie, which document order then breaks") is never exercised end-to-end: no test in packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.test.ts feeds two spans with EQUAL `at` to `computeBlameLabels` to check the document-order tiebreak that the clamp now relies on (the closest test, line 56, uses 99 vs 5). A tighter assertion (`at` close to now, and a gutter-level test where the forged run does not outrank a genuine later edit) would actually cover the behavior the test's comment claims.
searchedFor: read the three new clamp/sanitize tests
read computeBlameLabels tests for equal-`at` cases
read authorOfRange tiebreak logic in blame-gutter.ts

finding.summary: No test enables the blame gutter at runtime (`setShowAuthors(true)`), which is the only path the toolbar actually uses
finding.evidence: The editor-level tests cover (a) mounting with `showAuthors: false` (line 94-104), (b) mounting with `showAuthors: true` (line 106), and (c) turning it OFF from on (line 123-124). The production path is the opposite direction: notes-detail/notes-view mount with `readShowAuthors()` (default false) and then call `editor.setShowAuthors(true)` when the user checks "Show authors" in the view menu (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-view.tsx effect on `showAuthors`). That direction requires the two compartments to reconfigure, the tracker plugin to be constructed on an existing view, publish labels into `labelsByView`, and schedule the microtask repaint — none of which is asserted anywhere. A regression that leaves the freshly-enabled gutter permanently blank would keep the whole suite green.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists. packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.test.ts:106-141 ("switches the gutter on after mount, the way the view menu does") mounts the editor with showAuthors off (line 118, matching the production host path), asserts no .cm-noteBlame gutter yet (line 120), then calls api.setShowAuthors(true) (line 122) and asserts the real DOM gutter labels rendered: expect(gutterLabels(container)).toEqual(['ann','','bob']) (line 126), where gutterLabels reads '.cm-noteBlame .cm-gutterElement' textContent (lines 21-25). It further dispatches a real input on the live EditorView and asserts the new line is attributed to 'cal' (lines 130-137), proving the tracker installed by the reconfigure is live rather than a one-shot paint. Nothing is mocked: MemNoteStore is the real store and initialize builds a real CodeMirror view whose setShowAuthors reconfigures both blameGutterCompartment and blameTrackerCompartment (packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:517-526). A regression leaving the freshly-enabled gutter blank would fail this test, so the suite would not stay green. The finding's evidence also misreads the file: lines 122-137 are the ON direction; the OFF direction is a separate test at lines 143-165.
